2. Class Diagram and Interface Specification

a. Class Diagram

The class diagram refines the design objects that appeared as lifelines in the Part One sequence diagrams (Figures 1–5 in Section 1) into a single static model. Every lifeline there is a class here, and the messages exchanged in those diagrams are the operations listed in the class compartments. Where a lifeline hid a family of implementations (the two search indexes behind SearchIndex, the model vendors behind LlmProvider, the platform crawlers behind SourceCrawler), the family is now shown explicitly as an interface with its realisations. The classes are also checked against the implemented prototype in the project repository (lib/engine, lib/retrieval, lib/llm, lib/kb, lib/crawl, lib/log, components/chat), so the names in this section are the names a reader will find in the code.

Because the full model has 36 classes, it is presented the way the course format asks: Figure 6 is an overview that shows every class and every association but only the name compartment, grouped into six packages. Figures 7–10 are partial diagrams that show the three compartments (name, attributes, operations) for the classes of one use-case group each. In the diagrams only the visibility of each member is shown (+ public, − private); the data types and full operation signatures are given in Section 2b. Associations are read in the direction of the arrow; a hollow triangle with a dashed line is interface realisation; a filled diamond is composition (the part cannot exist without the whole); a hollow diamond is aggregation; a dashed arrow labelled creates is a dependency where the source constructs the target.

How the partial diagrams fit into the overview. The six packages of Figure 6 are the key. Boundary (ChatUI, TelegramBot) and Control (QAController, RefreshController) sit on the left of the overview; the citizen-facing partial diagrams A, B and C all start from them. Services and SearchAndModel are split between partial A (LanguageService, RetrievalService, SearchIndex and its two indexes) and partial B (AIModelGateway, LlmProvider and its providers, AnswerVerifier, CitationPresenter). KnowledgeAndConversation is spread over A (ContentStore, Passage, Candidate, ConversationHistory, Conversation, Question), B (Answer, SourceCitation, FeedbackLog, Report) and C (OfficeDirectory, ContactInfo). ContentRefresh is partial D in full. Classes that appear in more than one partial diagram are the joins between them: QAController appears in A, B and C; ChatUI in A, B and C; ContentStore in A and D (retrieval reads it, the refresh writes it after steward approval); ConversationHistory in A and C; Passage in A and B; and RegisteredSource in C and D. Where a class is repeated, the later diagram shows only the members that matter for that use case, and the full member list is the one in the first diagram that shows it.

Figure 6: Overview class diagram of SuperAsk.AI. All 36 classes and their associations, name compartment only, grouped into six packages.

The overview follows the four responsibility-assignment decisions of Part One. The two Controller classes are the only entry points from the boundary: everything the web chat or the Telegram bot does passes through QAController, and everything the Scheduler starts passes through RefreshController. The Information Expert classes (ContentStore, ConversationHistory, SourceRegistry, OfficeDirectory) own the data they answer questions about. The Pure Fabrication services (LanguageService, RetrievalService, AnswerVerifier, CitationPresenter) hold behaviour that belongs to no entity. The three interfaces (SearchIndex, LlmProvider, SourceCrawler) are the Protected Variations points: a new search method, model vendor, or source platform is a new realisation of one interface and nothing else changes, which is what REQ-29 and REQ-30 require.

Figure 7: Partial class diagram A: question handling and retrieval (UC-1 AskQuestion, UC-2 RetrieveOfficialSources, UC-6, UC-8, UC-9, UC-10).

ChatUI and TelegramBot are the two boundary classes (REQ-1, REQ-15); both create a Question and hand it to QAController. QAController keeps the two thresholds that decide the flow: a curated answer is served word-for-word when the match score is at least curatedThreshold, and retrieval results below retrievalMinScore trigger UC-4 instead of generation (REQ-7). LanguageService handles Khmer/English detection and normalisation (REQ-2, REQ-3). RetrievalService drives exactly two SearchIndex realisations, a KeywordIndex (BM25) and a VectorIndex (embeddings), fuses and reranks their results into Candidates, and asks ContentStore to drop passages that are no longer in effect (REQ-4, REQ-5). ConversationHistory stores Conversations for UC-6 and supplies the context RetrievalService needs to rewrite a follow-up question (UC-8, REQ-14).

Figure 8: Partial class diagram B: answer generation, verification, citation and feedback (UC-1, UC-3 ViewSourceCitation, UC-4).

AIModelGateway is the only class that talks to an AI model; it selects one LlmProvider realisation (AnthropicProvider or SeaLionProvider) and falls back to ExtractiveProvider, which quotes the best passage verbatim, when the model service is unavailable (UC-1 extension 7a). AnswerVerifier checks every fee, date and document in the draft against the cited passages before it creates the Answer (REQ-22); an Answer is composed of its SourceCitations, each of which cites exactly one Passage (REQ-6). CitationPresenter renders the citations as cards visually separate from the answer text and flags any citation past its review date (REQ-28, UC-3 extension 2a). FeedbackLog creates a Report when the citizen flags an answer and also writes the audit record for every answer served.

Figure 9: Partial class diagram C: office contact and location (UC-7 GetOfficeContactAndLocation).

QAController asks ConversationHistory which procedure “this” refers to, then asks OfficeDirectory for the responsible office. OfficeDirectory aggregates the ContactInfo records (today loaded from data/facilities.json) and also holds the emergency numbers. Each ContactInfo may point to the RegisteredSource it was verified from (REQ-11, REQ-12); when no verified online contact exists, OfficeDirectory returns the location only and the ChatUI shows the “no verified online contact” notice (REQ-13, REQ-39).

Figure 10: Partial class diagram D: scheduled content refresh with steward review (UC-11 RefreshOfficialContent).

RefreshController loads the RegisteredSources from SourceRegistry, calls fetchLatest on the SourceCrawler realisation matching each source's platform, and compares what comes back with ContentStore. A detected change becomes a ChangeSignal in the ReviewQueue; only when a human steward approves it does ReviewQueue call storeContent on ContentStore and reindex. The crawler classes never write to ContentStore directly, which is the design rule that keeps machine-fetched text out of citizen answers. RefreshController creates the RefreshReport from the counts it accumulated during the run (sources attempted and reachable, pages fetched, blocked by robots.txt, rejected as block pages, changes, errors).

b. Data Types and Operation Signatures

The specification below is written independently of the diagrams, in UML notation, with one table per class. Attribute types use the UML primitives (String, Integer, Real, Boolean, Date) plus List<T> and Map<K,V>; enumerations are written as a set of literals. A few small value types are shared by several classes and are defined once first.

Shared value types

TypeDefinitionMeaning
Langenumeration {km, en}Language of a question, answer, or interface text.
Tierenumeration {1, 2, 3}How the answer was produced: 1 curated human-approved answer, 2 retrieval-augmented generation, 3 refusal.
Freshnessenumeration {fresh, due, stale}Whether a passage's last-verified date is within, at, or past its review date.
Confidenceenumeration {high, medium, low}The model's self-reported confidence; low confidence forces a decline.
Turnstructure {role: enumeration {user, assistant}, text: String}One message of a conversation, used as history context.
RetrievalResultstructure {query: ProcessedQuery, candidates: List<Candidate>, topScore: Real}What RetrievalService returns; topScore is the best rerank score, normalised 0–1, and drives the confidence gate.
ProcessedQuerystructure {raw: String, normalised: String, segments: List<String>, expanded: List<String>, romanised: Boolean, rewritten: String}The question after normalisation, segmentation, alias expansion and (for follow-ups) rewriting.
GenerationRequeststructure {question: String, lang: Lang, mode: enumeration {grounded, general}, sources: List<Passage>, history: List<Turn>}Everything a model provider needs to write an answer; grounded is the default and restricts the model to the supplied passages.
GenerationResultstructure {answer: String, citations: List<String>, confidence: Confidence, shouldDecline: Boolean}The draft answer with the passage ids it rests on.
VerificationResultstructure {passed: Boolean, unsupported: List<String>, invalidCitations: List<String>}Outcome of the claim check: claims with no supporting passage, and cited ids that were never retrieved.
GuardrailHitstructure {kind: String, message: String}Why a question or answer was stopped by a guardrail (emergency, legal advice, political, out of scope, moderation).
FetchResultstructure {status: Integer, body: String, fetchedAt: Date, blocked: Boolean, error: String}What a crawler got back from an official source.
CrawlOptionsstructure {mode: enumeration {verify, monitor}, priorities: List<Integer>}Which sources a refresh run covers; the weekly run uses mode monitor and priorities 1 and 2.

ChatUI — boundary. The web chat interface (React components under components/chat). It collects the question, shows the answer, citations, contact card or decline notice, and forwards reports. It holds no business logic.

AttributeTypeMeaning
languageLangInterface language chosen by the user (UC-10).
conversationIdStringId of the conversation currently shown.
messagesList<Turn>Turns displayed in the chat pane.
isLoadingBooleanTrue while a question is being answered; shows the loading indicator.
OperationMeaning
+enterQuestion(text: String): voidPuts the typed text into the input field; empty text keeps the send button disabled (UC-1 2a).
+submitQuestion(): voidBuilds a Question from the input and the recent turns and calls QAController.askQuestion.
+displayAnswer(answer: Answer): voidRenders the answer text in the question's language with steps, documents, fees, deadlines and hours.
+displayDecline(coveredAreas: List<String>): voidShows the “cannot answer” message with the areas SuperAsk.AI does cover (UC-4).
+displaySourceCitation(answer: Answer): voidAsks CitationPresenter to render the Verified Source cards under the answer (UC-3).
+showContactCard(contact: ContactInfo): voidShows name, address, hours, phone and the Google Maps link (UC-7).
+openOfficialSource(url: String): voidOpens the cited official page in a new tab.
+reportAnswer(answerId: String, comment: String): voidForwards a citizen's “this is incorrect” report to FeedbackLog.
+switchLanguage(lang: Lang): voidSwitches interface text between Khmer and English (UC-10).
+selectPopularProcedure(name: String): voidSends a sidebar procedure as a question (UC-5).

TelegramBot — boundary. The Telegram channel (webhook route plus lib/telegram). It receives updates from the Telegram Bot API, turns them into Questions for QAController, and sends the answer back as a message. It also offers the Mini App button that opens ChatUI inside Telegram (UC-9).

AttributeTypeMeaning
botTokenStringBot API credential, held server-side only (REQ-27).
webhookSecretStringSecret Telegram must present on every webhook call.
miniAppUrlStringPublic URL of ChatUI embedded as the Mini App.
OperationMeaning
+handleUpdate(update: TelegramUpdate): voidValidates the secret, extracts chat id and text, appends the turn to ConversationHistory and calls QAController.askQuestion.
+sendReply(chatId: Integer, answer: Answer): voidFormats the Answer and its citations as a Telegram message and sends it.
+sendChatAction(chatId: Integer): voidShows the “typing” indicator while the answer is produced.
+channelKeyboard(): ReplyMarkupBuilds the keyboard with the Open SuperAsk (Mini App) button.

Question — entity. A citizen's question as submitted through any channel (the AskRequest contract in the code).

AttributeTypeMeaning
textStringThe question in Khmer, English or mixed.
languageLangDetected by LanguageService; answers come back in this language.
historyList<Turn>Recent turns of the same conversation, for follow-up resolution (UC-8).
sessionIdStringCorrelates the question with its audit record.

No operations (data class; accessed through its attributes).

QAController — control. Use-case controller for all citizen-facing flows (UC-1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8). Runs the fixed pipeline guardrail screen → curated match → retrieval → confidence gate → generation → verification → output moderation → citation assembly (lib/engine/tiers.ts).

AttributeTypeMeaning
curatedThresholdRealMinimum match score for a Tier 1 curated answer to be served verbatim (0.72).
retrievalMinScoreRealDecline floor: if the top rerank score is below it the question goes to UC-4 (0.20).
OperationMeaning
+askQuestion(request: Question): AnswerMain operation of UC-1; returns a sourced Answer, a curated answer, or a decline.
+getOfficeContact(request: Question): AnswerUC-7: resolves the procedure, finds the office and returns an Answer whose office field holds the ContactInfo.
−screenGuardrails(question: String): GuardrailHitPolicy screen that runs before any retrieval (emergency, legal advice, political, chit-chat); null when the question may proceed.
−matchCurated(question: String, lang: Lang): CuratedMatchLooks for a human-approved Tier 1 answer; null when none scores above curatedThreshold.
−checkScope(question: String): BooleanTrue when the question is about a government service (UC-1 5a).
−confidenceGate(result: RetrievalResult): BooleanTrue when result.topScore ≥ retrievalMinScore; false sends the flow to UC-4.
−moderateOutput(answer: String): GuardrailHitChecks the generated text before it is shown; null when clean.
−buildDecline(reason: String): AnswerBuilds the Tier 3 Answer with the decline text, covered areas and coverageGap = true.

RefreshController — control. Use-case controller for UC-11. Started by the Scheduler (a weekly scheduled task), it coordinates the crawl of every registered source, change detection, queueing for steward review, and the run report (lib/crawl/crawl.ts).

AttributeTypeMeaning
modeenumeration {verify, monitor}verify probes that a source is reachable; monitor fetches content and detects changes.
prioritiesList<Integer>Which source priorities this run covers (weekly run: 1 and 2).
startedAtDateStart time, copied into the RefreshReport.
OperationMeaning
+startRefresh(options: CrawlOptions): RefreshReportRuns the whole refresh and returns the report.
−compareWithStored(source: RegisteredSource, snapshot: SourceSnapshot): List<ChangeSignal>Compares fetched text hashes with the stored snapshot; one ChangeSignal per new, modified, removed or unreachable page.
−classifyChange(diff: String): enumeration {factual, presentation}Keyword scan for fees, deadlines, documents, eligibility and steps; factual changes always need steward approval.
−createReport(): RefreshReportCreates the RefreshReport from the counts gathered during the run.

LanguageService — service. Khmer/English handling in one place (lib/lang, lib/khmer): detection, Unicode normalisation, segmentation and romanised-Khmer mapping.

No attributes.

OperationMeaning
+detectLanguage(text: String): Langkm when the text contains Khmer script, otherwise en.
+normalise(text: String): StringUnicode normalisation and canonical reordering of Khmer clusters; case folding for Latin.
+segment(text: String): List<String>Splits Khmer (no spaces) and English text into search terms.
+romanisedToKhmer(text: String): StringMaps romanised Khmer typed on a Latin keyboard to Khmer script.
+khmerDigitsToAscii(text: String): StringConverts Khmer numerals so fees and dates compare correctly.

RetrievalService — service. Hybrid retrieval over the approved content (lib/retrieval): query processing, keyword and vector search, reciprocal-rank fusion, reranking and the effective-content filter (UC-2).

AttributeTypeMeaning
topKIntegerNumber of reranked candidates returned (8).
anchorLookbackIntegerHow many earlier turns are searched for the subject of a follow-up question (4).
OperationMeaning
+retrievePassages(question: String, history: List<Turn>, topK: Integer): RetrievalResultMain operation of UC-2; returns the ranked candidates with their passages and the top score.
−processQuery(question: String, history: List<Turn>): ProcessedQueryNormalises, segments, expands aliases and, for an anaphoric follow-up, rewrites the question.
−rewriteQueryWithContext(question: String, history: List<Turn>): StringReplaces “it”/“this” with the subject named in an earlier turn (UC-2 2a).
−normaliseAndExpand(query: String): List<String>Adds known synonyms and abbreviations such as MPWT.
−mergeAndRerank(lexical: Map<String,Real>, dense: Map<String,Real>): List<Candidate>Reciprocal-rank fusion of the two score maps followed by a cross-encoder style rerank.

SearchIndex — interface. Common interface of the two search methods, so RetrievalService does not depend on either (Polymorphism, Protected Variations). Both realisations take the same ProcessedQuery and each reads the part of it that it needs, so RetrievalService calls them identically.

No attributes.

OperationMeaning
+build(passages: List<Passage>): voidIndexes the given passages.
+search(query: ProcessedQuery): Map<String,Real>Returns passage id → score for the processed query.

KeywordIndex — class (realises SearchIndex). BM25 keyword index (lib/retrieval/bm25.ts).

AttributeTypeMeaning
k1RealBM25 term-frequency saturation parameter.
bRealBM25 length-normalisation parameter.
avgDocLengthRealAverage passage length in terms.
postingsMap<String, Map<String,Integer>>term → (passage id → term frequency).
OperationMeaning
+build(passages: List<Passage>): voidBuilds the postings from passage text, keywords and candidate questions.
+search(query: ProcessedQuery): Map<String,Real>BM25 score per passage, using query.segments and query.expanded as the search terms.
−idf(term: String): RealInverse document frequency of a term.

VectorIndex — class (realises SearchIndex). Meaning-based index over passage embeddings (lib/retrieval/embed.ts).

AttributeTypeMeaning
dimensionsIntegerEmbedding size.
vectorsMap<String, List<Real>>passage id → embedding.
OperationMeaning
+build(passages: List<Passage>): voidEmbeds every passage.
+search(query: ProcessedQuery): Map<String,Real>Embeds query.rewritten (or query.normalised when there is no rewrite) and returns the cosine similarity to each passage.
−embed(text: String): List<Real>Produces the embedding of a text.
−cosine(a: List<Real>, b: List<Real>): RealCosine similarity of two vectors.

AIModelGateway — service. The only class that calls an external AI model (lib/llm). Chooses the configured LlmProvider, builds the versioned grounding prompt, parses the JSON reply and falls back to ExtractiveProvider on failure (Indirection, Protected Variations).

AttributeTypeMeaning
providerLlmProviderConfigured model provider.
fallbackProviderLlmProviderExtractiveProvider, used when the configured provider fails or times out (UC-1 7a).
promptVersionStringVersion of the grounding prompt, logged with every answer (grounding-v6).
OperationMeaning
+generateAnswer(question: String, passages: List<Passage>, lang: Lang, history: List<Turn>): GenerationResultWrites an answer using only the supplied passages and returns the ids it cited.
+describeProvider(): ProviderInfoProvider id, model, hosting and data residency, for diagnostics.
−buildPrompt(request: GenerationRequest): StringAssembles the system prompt, the SOURCES block and the JSON contract.
−parseGeneration(raw: String): GenerationResultParses the model's JSON reply; a malformed reply counts as a failure.

LlmProvider — interface. Common interface of all model providers.

AttributeTypeMeaning
infoProviderInfoStatic description of the provider (id, label, model, hosting, residency).
OperationMeaning
+generate(request: GenerationRequest): GenerationResultProduces a draft answer for the request.

AnthropicProvider — class (realises LlmProvider). Provider that calls the Anthropic Claude API.

AttributeTypeMeaning

OperationMeaning

SeaLionProvider — class (realises LlmProvider). Provider for a self-hosted or regional model endpoint (SEA-LION / vLLM), kept for data-residency experiments.

AttributeTypeMeaning

OperationMeaning
+generate(request: GenerationRequest): GenerationResultSends the prompt to the endpoint and parses the reply.

ExtractiveProvider — class (realises LlmProvider). Deterministic fallback that needs no credential: it returns the most relevant retrieved passage word for word, with its citation.

No attributes.

OperationMeaning

AnswerVerifier — service. Checks that every fee, date, document and number in the draft appears in a cited passage, then creates the Answer (lib/engine/verify.ts; REQ-22).

No attributes.

OperationMeaning
+verifyClaims(draft: String, citedIds: List<String>, citedPassages: List<Passage>, retrievedIds: List<String>): VerificationResultReturns passed = false with the unsupported claims when a claim has no source, or when a cited id was never retrieved.
+createAnswer(draft: String, citations: List<SourceCitation>, lang: Lang): AnswerCreates the final Answer object (Creator).
−extractClaims(text: String): List<String>Pulls amounts, dates, durations and document names out of the draft.

c. Traceability Matrix

Report One did not contain a separate domain model, so the domain concepts traced here are the nouns of Report One itself: the things named in the use-case descriptions (Section 3c), the fully-dressed use cases (3c-iv), the system sequence diagrams (3d) and the requirements (Section 2). Each row names one such concept, the design class or classes it became, and why the name or the number of classes changed. Classes that appear in no row (KeywordIndex, VectorIndex, Candidate, AnthropicProvider, SeaLionProvider, ExtractiveProvider, WebsiteCrawler, FacebookCrawler, TelegramCrawler) are realisations or working data that exist only because of a design decision, and they are explained with the concept they serve.

Traceability (1): domain concepts of Report One to design classes

Domain concept (Report One)Design class(es)Why the name or the number of classes changed
Citizen's question (UC-1 steps 1–2; REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-31, REQ-32)Question, ChatUI, TelegramBotThe question itself became the Question entity. The “chat interface” and “messaging channel” of REQ-1 and REQ-15 became two boundary classes, ChatUI and TelegramBot, because they share nothing but the Question they create and the Answer they display. Messenger (REQ-15) would be a third boundary class with the same two responsibilities.
SuperAsk.AI as a black box (3d system sequence diagrams)QAController, RefreshController, LanguageService, RetrievalService, AIModelGateway, AnswerVerifier, CitationPresenterThe black box was opened in Part One into one controller per initiating actor (QAController for the citizen, RefreshController for the Scheduler) and the Pure Fabrication services that hold the behaviour the black box performed in steps 4–9 of UC-1: language detection (LanguageService), lookup (RetrievalService), writing (AIModelGateway), checking (AnswerVerifier) and displaying sources (CitationPresenter). Splitting them keeps each class cohesive and makes the pipeline order in QAController visible.
Language detection and Khmer handling (UC-1 step 4; REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-26, REQ-37)LanguageService; Lang typeNamed after its single responsibility. The language value became a shared Lang type carried by Question, Answer and ChatUI rather than an attribute of one class.
Stored official content / official passages (UC-2 steps 2–6; REQ-4, REQ-5, REQ-29)ContentStore, PassageOne concept became two classes: Passage is the unit of content with its provenance (ministry, instrument, article, effective and verified dates), and ContentStore is the Information Expert that holds all passages and decides which are currently in effect. REQ-29 is why the content is data in the store, not code.
Keyword search and meaning-based search (UC-2 step 2)SearchIndex (interface), KeywordIndex, VectorIndex, CandidateThe two search methods of the use case became two realisations of one SearchIndex interface so RetrievalService depends on neither. Candidate did not exist as a domain concept; it is the working record that carries the two scores, the fused score and the rerank score through step 3 (merge and re-rank) to the confidence gate.
AI Model Service (participating actor of UC-1; UC-1 step 7, 7a)AIModelGateway, LlmProvider (interface), AnthropicProvider, SeaLionProvider, ExtractiveProviderThe external actor stays external; what the system owns is the gateway that talks to it. The gateway was given a provider interface with three realisations so the model vendor can change without touching the pipeline (Protected Variations), and so the 7a fallback (“show the most relevant passage word for word”) is just another provider, ExtractiveProvider.
Answer with steps, documents, fees, deadlines, hours (UC-1 step 9; REQ-16 to REQ-20, REQ-33)AnswerKept as one entity. Tier, coverageGap and unverified were added because the use-case extensions (curated answer, UC-4 decline, model fallback) are all Answers of a different kind rather than different classes.
Verified source / citation (UC-3; REQ-6, REQ-28, REQ-34)SourceCitation, CitationPresenterThe “Verified Source card” concept split into the data (SourceCitation, composed into Answer) and the behaviour of showing it separately from the answer text and flagging an outdated one (CitationPresenter). The split keeps REQ-28 in one class.
Claim check (UC-1 step 8, 8a; REQ-22)AnswerVerifierBecame its own class because it is the safety gate of the whole system and is tested on its own; it also creates the Answer because it already holds the draft and the citations (Creator).
Recent conversations and conversation context (UC-6, UC-8; REQ-10, REQ-14, REQ-36)ConversationHistory, Conversation, Turn typeThe list of recent conversations became ConversationHistory (the expert that lists, stores and resolves references) holding Conversation entities made of Turns. One class serves both the web (browser storage) and Telegram (server memory), which is why it is an abstraction rather than a UI component.
Ministry / responsible office, contact and location (UC-7; REQ-11, REQ-12, REQ-13, REQ-20, REQ-38, REQ-39)OfficeDirectory, ContactInfoThe office became ContactInfo (the record) and OfficeDirectory (the expert that finds the responsible office and knows when nothing verified exists, so it never guesses). The Google Maps link became the mapLink attribute.
Report of incorrect information (UC-3 3a)Report, FeedbackLogThe citizen's report became a Report entity created by FeedbackLog. FeedbackLog also absorbed the audit trail of answers, which Report One mentions only indirectly through REQ-22 acceptance testing, because they are the same append-only, redacted log mechanism.
Registered official sources: ministry websites, Facebook pages, Telegram channels (UC-11 precondition, steps 2–4; REQ-8, REQ-30)SourceRegistry, RegisteredSource, SourceCrawler (interface), WebsiteCrawler, FacebookCrawler, TelegramCrawlerThe source list became SourceRegistry (expert) holding RegisteredSource entries. The three platforms named in Report One became three realisations of one SourceCrawler interface, so a fourth platform is one new class. Only WebsiteCrawler is implemented so far; the other two are in the diagram because the use case names them.
Comparing with the stored copy and saving changed text (UC-11 steps 6–7)ChangeSignal, ReviewQueue, ContentStore.storeContentReport One let the system save changed text directly. The design inserts a human step: a change becomes a ChangeSignal in a ReviewQueue, and only an approved change reaches ContentStore. This was added because the implementation review found that a crawler fetching a page is not a steward approving it, and it is the mechanism behind the “steward review” note in the UC-11 sequence diagram.
Refresh report (UC-11 step 9)RefreshReportKept as one entity, created by RefreshController, with the counts the use case lists plus the robots and block-page counts from extensions 3a and 4b.
Scheduler (initiating actor of UC-11)no classRemains an actor outside the system: a weekly scheduled task on a team machine that runs RefreshController.startRefresh. It owns no data and no behaviour of SuperAsk.AI.

The second matrix reads the other way, from design classes to the use cases of Report One (Section 3c-i), so that every class can be seen to serve at least one use case and the five demonstration use cases (UC-1, 2, 3, 7, 11) can be seen to be covered end to end. QAController, ContentStore, ConversationHistory and Answer appear in the most columns because they are the shared backbone of the citizen-facing flows; RefreshController and the refresh entities appear only in UC-11, which is why the refresh runs as a separate process from the web server (Section 3).

Review notes for the rest of the Part 2 tab (not for pasting)

  1. Empty headings. 3a Identifying Subsystems, 3b Architecture Styles and 3c Mapping Subsystems to Hardware have no text yet. Suggested subsystems, matching the packages of Figure 1 and the code folders: Citizen Interface (web chat, Telegram bot and Mini App), Question-Answer Engine (controller, language, retrieval, generation, verification), Knowledge Base (content store, office directory, curated answers), Content Monitoring (registry, crawlers, review queue), and Logging (audit, feedback). Styles that fit: client–server over HTTPS, a layered pipeline inside the engine, and event-driven for the two entry points (user request, scheduler tick).
  2. Class names. Section 3 already uses QAController, RetrievalService, AIModelGateway, RefreshController, SourceCrawler, ConversationHistory and Scheduler. These match Section 2, so nothing needs renaming.
  3. 3d Connectors and Network Protocols. The text is right but names no protocol. Add: the web chat calls the backend over HTTPS with JSON bodies (POST /api/ask, POST /api/feedback, GET /api/health); Telegram delivers messages by HTTPS webhook (Telegram Bot API → POST /api/telegram/webhook, checked with a shared secret) and replies go back through the Bot API over HTTPS; the Mini App is the same /chat page loaded inside Telegram (the page allows telegram.org as a frame ancestor); the AI model is called over HTTPS JSON (Anthropic SDK); the crawler uses HTTP(S) GET with a SuperAskBot user agent, respects robots.txt and waits 2 s between requests to the same host. Request and response bodies are limited to 4.5 MB by the host.
  4. 3e Global Control Flow. Add one sentence that the refresh is not run by the web server: it is a weekly Windows scheduled task (Sunday 02:00 ICT, scripts/schedule-weekly.ps1) on a team machine, so the two flows never compete for the same process. Time dependency: the Telegram webhook is capped at 60 s per update and ordinary requests at 300 s by the host; the 5 s target of REQ-24 is dominated by the model call (retrieval runs in milliseconds).
  5. 3f Hardware Requirements: replace with specific minimums. The current text says “sufficient CPU and RAM” without numbers. Suggested replacement is below.
  6. Data storage caveat. Audit and feedback logs are append-only files under var/. On the Vercel host the file system is not persistent, so these logs do not survive a redeploy; the architecture section should say that a database or log service is required for production. The knowledge base itself is in the repository, so it is safe.
  7. Figure numbers. Section 2 uses Figures 1–5. Any figure in Section 3 should start at Figure 6.
  8. Contributions table. Suggested row: “Phallamonunhh Chun — Contributed to Section 2: Class Diagram and Interface Specification; derived the design classes from the Part One sequence diagrams and the implemented code, specified data types and operation signatures, and traced the classes to Report One's domain concepts and use cases.”

Suggested replacement for 3f Hardware Requirements

Client. Any phone, tablet or computer with a current browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox or Edge) and a Khmer Unicode font, which Android, iOS and Windows include by default (REQ-26). The web interface is laid out for screens from 360 pixels wide up to desktop resolutions (REQ-25). Telegram users need the Telegram app; the Mini App opens the same web interface inside it. A question and its answer with citations is under 50 KB of JSON, so a basic mobile data connection of about 1 Mbps is enough; no client-side storage beyond the browser's local storage for recent conversations is used.

Server. The prototype runs on Vercel's serverless platform with Node.js 24 and Next.js 15. Each request runs in a function with 1 vCPU and 2 GB of memory and must finish within 300 s (the Telegram webhook is configured to 60 s). The knowledge base is small: 664 KB on disk, 45 approved passages from four organisations and 132 registered sources, loaded from disk and indexed in memory (keyword and vector index) when a function starts; this uses well under 100 MB of memory and leaves room for a knowledge base a hundred times larger. The deployment bundle must stay under 250 MB and request and response bodies under 4.5 MB. A self-hosted equivalent therefore needs at minimum 1 vCPU, 1 GB of RAM (2 GB recommended), 1 GB of disk for the application build, the knowledge base and the append-only logs, a public HTTPS address (required for the Telegram webhook), and outbound HTTPS to the AI model API and the Telegram Bot API.

Content-refresh machine. The weekly refresh (UC-11) runs as a scheduled task on a team member's computer, not on the web host. It needs Node.js 24, 2 GB of RAM, about 1 GB of disk that grows with the retained copies of fetched pages (at most 5 MB per page), and an ordinary internet connection: with a 20 s timeout per request and a 2 s politeness delay per host, the 132 registered sources complete well within the task's 4-hour limit.

External services. The AI model API (Anthropic) and the Telegram Bot API. Credentials for both are held only in server-side environment variables (REQ-27). Without a model credential the system still runs, using the extractive fallback provider.
